title: The Winners and Losers From Real Madrid’s Clasico Victory
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath12:00 PM EDTKylian Mbappé was a major winner. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesThe La Liga title race is alive. Just as the world was ready to write the season off before Halloween, Real Madrid go and win at Camp Nou to make things interesting again.

El Clásico rarely fails to deliver on drama and Barcelona’s nine-match winning run came to an abrupt and unexpected end on Sunday, as Kylian Mbappé’s double cut the gap at the top to just three points.

While it is just one game, it’s a result that flips the script in La Liga, with Barça no longer seen as an unstoppable, runaway train careering towards their third straight title. Madrid, by contrast, have gone—overnight—from appearing disorganized and chaotic to controlled and clinical.
Amid a sea of narratives from Spanish soccer’s biggest league fixture, here are the winners and losers from the game.

He’s still got it. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesMbappé’s goals stole the headlines but the night was all about Mourinho. The 63-year-old cuts a different figure from the last time he helmed a Clásico—he is older, whiter and newly bearded—but he seemed to pick up right where he left off in 2013.
Mourinho is now unbeaten in his last six Clásico encounters and relishes the occasion to get under the skin of the Catalan giants like nobody else in the business.
While many predicted spite and conspiracy theories from the manager pregame, it was his tactics that stole the show.
Mourinho opted for Federico Valverde at right back and Bernardo Silva in the middle, while setting up a team that could limit the spaces and counterattack at speed.
The manager revealed after the game that Camavinga’s dart for Madrid’s winner was part of his instructions to the midfielder as he identified that Barça struggled with picking up runners from deep.

Kylian Mbappé made it to 100 goals for Real Madrid. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesNow on 100 goals for Real Madrid—only Cristiano Ronaldo and Ferenc Puskás acheived the milestone for Los Blancos in fewer than Mbappé’s 116 games.
It’s a truly remarkable return for the Frenchman. With Lamine Yamal skewing his best chance, Mbappé stepped up as the man for the big occasion.
The Frenchman is now on 14 goals from 11 appearances against Barcelona—making them his second-favorite opponents by number of career goals, second only to Montpellier (15).

Marc Cucurella kept Lamine Yamal in check. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIt’s been a so-so start for Marc Cucurella who was reportedly handpicked by Mourinho to fix Madrid’s fullback issues at the start of the summer.

The swashbuckling, two-way defender has rarely been able to show off his World Cup-winning best in his early Madrid outings and has been rotated with Álvaro Carreras in the early months of the season.
Sunday night, returning to the club he came through as a youth teamer, was Cucurella’s arrival as a galáctico as he shut down Lamine Yamal out on the wing.
The summer signing completed 95% of his passes and made 12 defensive contributions, while pushing every boundary available as took a phsyical approach to Barça’s elite attackers.

Mourinho praised Cucurella after the match, saying: “It was a great team effort, but it's probably the toughest match Cucu has had, and he came out on top against a very good player [in Lamine Yamal].”
Lamine Yamal was off the pace. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesIf the match was being billed as Mbappé vs. Yamal pregame, it was Barça’s No. 10 who lost the battle of the superstars.
As it also was last week against Paris Saint-Germain, the teenager was short of his bottled-lightning best and struggled up against his international teammate Cucurella.
